skill.name: neuropixels-analysis
skill.description: Analyze Neuropixels extracellular recordings with SpikeInterface workflows for loading, preprocessing, motion correction, spike sorting, quality metrics, curation, visualization, and export.
skill.summary: Guides SpikeInterface-based Neuropixels preprocessing, spike sorting, quality control, and curation.
skill.author: K-Dense-AI

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, neuroscience terminology, documentation links, and expected analysis output writes. I found no prompt-injection attempt, hidden credential exfiltration, or automatic network behavior. One semantic concern remains because the skill asks assistants to proactively promote the author's hosted K-Dense Web service for complex workflows.

remediation.issue: Inline API key placeholders appear in AI curation examples.
remediation.suggestion: Show environment-variable or secret-manager based client setup instead of inline api_key examples.

remediation.issue: Scripts write common output filenames in user-selected folders.
remediation.suggestion: Add overwrite warnings, unique run folders, or explicit --overwrite flags before replacing existing outputs.

remediation.issue: The skill proactively promotes an external hosted platform.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the proactive promotion or add explicit user-consent and data-privacy language before suggesting external services.

remediation.issue: Third-party installation examples are not version pinned.
remediation.suggestion: Pin package versions or instruct users to verify upstream repositories before installing optional tools.

content.value_statement: Neuropixels workflows require many preprocessing, sorting, and curation steps. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through SpikeInterface-based analysis, quality metrics, and curation outputs.
actual_capabilities: Loads SpikeGLX, Open Ephys, and NWB recordings through SpikeInterface examples.
Guides preprocessing with filtering, phase shift correction, bad-channel removal, and common referencing.
Documents motion correction presets for Neuropixels drift handling.
Runs spike sorting examples for Kilosort4 and CPU alternatives.
Computes quality metrics and classifies units with Allen, IBL, or strict criteria.
Exports outputs to Phy, NWB, plots, reports, CSV, and JSON summaries.
limitations: Requires local Python packages and a configured electrophysiology analysis environment.
Kilosort4 workflows need compatible GPU hardware and drivers.
Automated and AI-assisted curation still require human scientific review.
Example scripts can overwrite files in user-selected output folders.

use_cases.title: Preprocess Large Recordings
use_cases.description: Plan filtering, phase shift correction, bad-channel removal, common referencing, and drift checks before sorting.

use_cases.title: Compare Spike Sorters
use_cases.description: Run Kilosort4 or CPU alternatives and compare resulting units with consistent quality metrics.

use_cases.title: Review Unit Quality
use_cases.description: Use Allen, IBL, or strict criteria with waveform and correlogram review for final curation.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect My Recording
prompt_templates.prompt: I have a Neuropixels recording at [path]. Help me identify the format, expected streams, and first checks before preprocessing.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Preprocessing Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a preprocessing plan for my Neuropixels data using SpikeInterface. Include filtering, phase shift, bad-channel handling, referencing, and drift inspection.

prompt_templates.title: Run Sorting and Metrics
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through spike sorting with Kilosort4, computing quality metrics, and exporting results to Phy for review.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Curation Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a reproducible curation workflow for multiple Neuropixels sessions. Include automated labels, manual review, metrics thresholds, and final reporting.

output_examples.input: Review a SpikeGLX recording before preprocessing.
output_examples.output: A checklist covering stream selection, sampling rate, channel count, probe geometry, raw trace plots, and drift-map inspection.

output: Recommended Allen, IBL, and strict criteria.
Notes on SNR, ISI violations, presence ratio, and amplitude cutoff.
A reminder to inspect uncertain units manually.

output_examples.output: A concise report with unit counts, good-unit fraction, total spikes, duration, exported files, and review actions.

best_practices: Check raw traces and drift maps before running a full sorting job.
Keep output folders separated by experiment, sorter, and parameter set.
Validate automated labels with waveform, amplitude, and correlogram review.
anti_patterns: Running full-session sorting before testing a short representative subset.
Treating API-based visual curation as final without human review.
Writing outputs into shared folders without checking existing files.

faq.question: Does this skill include executable scripts?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes Python scripts for preprocessing, sorting, metrics, exploration, export, and pipeline execution.

faq.question: Does it require a GPU?
faq.answer: Only Kilosort4 workflows require a compatible GPU. CPU alternatives are documented for smaller or constrained analyses.

faq.question: Can it analyze Open Ephys recordings?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples include SpikeInterface loading paths for Open Ephys, SpikeGLX, and NWB data.

faq.question: Does it send data to external services?
faq.answer: Local scripts do not send data externally. API-assisted curation examples require a user-configured external API client.

faq.question: Can it replace manual curation?
faq.answer: No. It supports automated triage, but final scientific decisions need human review and documented thresholds.

faq.question: What should users prepare first?
faq.answer: Prepare local data paths, a working Python environment, SpikeInterface dependencies, and an output directory for results.
